:::{#thm-cross-product-sum-outer}
#### The cross-product matrix is the sum of the outer products of the rows

Let $\matr{A}$ be an $m \times n$ [matrix](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix) with rows $\tp{\vecf{r}_1}, \ldots, \tp{\vecf{r}_m}$.
Let $\matr{B}$ be an $m \times q$ matrix with rows $\tp{\vecf{s}_1}, \ldots, \tp{\vecf{s}_m}$.
Then the [cross-product matrix](#def-cross-product-matrix) of $\matr{A}$ with $\matr{B}$ is

$$
\tprod{\matr{A}}{\matr{B}} = \sumto{i}{m} \vecf{r}_i\,\tp{\vecf{s}_i}.
$$

:::

:::{.proof}
Compare entry $(j, k)$ of each side.

$$
\ba
\paren{\tprod{\matr{A}}{\matr{B}}}_{jk}
&= \sumto{i}{m} \paren{\matr{A}}_{ij} \paren{\matr{B}}_{ik}
&& \text{(@def-matrix-mult)}
\\
&= \sumto{i}{m} \paren{\vecf{r}_i}_j \paren{\vecf{s}_i}_k
&& \text{(entries of the rows)}
\\
&= \sumto{i}{m} \paren{\vecf{r}_i\,\tp{\vecf{s}_i}}_{jk}
&& \text{(@def-outer-product)}
\\
&= \paren{\sumto{i}{m} \vecf{r}_i\,\tp{\vecf{s}_i}}_{jk}.
&& \text{(entries of a sum)}
\ea
$$

Every entry agrees, so the two matrices agree.
:::
